properties.statement: THE STALE-SERVER DEFECT REPRODUCED FIRST-HAND IN THIS REPO, IN THE SESSION THAT CAPTURED IT — AND THE `/proc/self/exe` SIGNAL dev_storyflow PROPOSED WAS SITTING RIGHT THERE, TRUE, THE WHOLE TIME. Not reported by anyone: observed here on 2026-08-08 while running loop_status after a normal working session. WHAT WAS SEEN: `loop_status` returned a field, `open_defects: 90`, that WAS NOT IN THE RESPONSE AT SESSION START and DOES NOT EXIST ANYWHERE IN THE CHECKED-OUT SOURCE — `grep -rn open_defects crates/` returns nothing on this branch, and the branch that implements it (`feat/loop-reads-defect-facts`) is verified NOT an ancestor of HEAD. THE DIAGNOSIS, run rather than reasoned: `ps` showed the `--serve-shared` daemon started at 05:22 THAT MORNING, mid-session — the previous daemon had hit its idle timeout during the long `cargo test --workspace` runs and a replacement was auto-spawned from `target/debug/reflow2-mcp`, which at that moment still held a build made in an EARLIER session on a DIFFERENT branch. Confirmed by comparing the two binaries directly: `strings /proc/1345843/exe | grep -c open_defects` = 1, while `strings target/debug/reflow2-mcp | grep -c open_defects` = 0. The running server and the source being edited were built from different code, and NOTHING ANYWHERE SAID SO. THE PROPOSED FIX IS VALIDATED, not merely plausible: `readlink /proc/1345843/exe` returned `/home/ajs7/project/reflow2/target/debug/reflow2-mcp (deleted)` — the exact kernel marker w-6904efa6 proposed deriving `stale: true` from, present and correct at the moment it was needed, requiring one syscall and no second source. This is now confirmed on two machines, two projects, two independent incidents. WHAT IT COST HERE, stated rather than glossed: every computed rollup read after 05:22 — gap counts, structural_defects 1 to 3, open_defects itself — came from a build that is not the one being shipped. Graph WRITES were unaffected (the store is the store, and the export and gate were both computed from the working tree by `cargo`/`reflow2_check.py`, plus a clean-checkout CI run), so the deliverable stands; but any number quoted from the server mid-session is of unknown provenance, and a session that had reported one as evidence would have been wrong with no way to notice. THE SHARPEST PART: this happened in the very session that was capturing and fixing a defect of this class, to an agent that had just written the words 'the server can detect its own staleness with one syscall' — and it was still only caught because a field appeared that could not possibly exist. That is the argument for the field rather than the discipline.
